introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.
enonce_intro_markdown: The points $P$ and $Q$ have position vectors $3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$ and $2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$ respectively.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Write down the vector equation of the line $l_1$ passing through $P$ and $Q$ in the form $\mathbf{r}=\mathbf{a}+t\mathbf{b}$, where $t$ is a scalar. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Direction vector: $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p}=(2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})=-\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$.

Starting at $P$:

**$l_1:\ \mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+t(-\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})$** (any equivalent form, for example starting at $Q$ or with direction $\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$, is correct).

questions.enonce_markdown: Another line, $l_2$, has vector equation $l_2:\ \mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+s(5\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$, where $s$ is also a scalar. Find: (b) the position vector of the point of intersection of the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the intersection the $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ components are equal:

- $\mathbf{i}$: $3-t=2+5s$
- $\mathbf{j}$: $-2+5t=3+s$

From the first, $t=1-5s$. Substitute in the second: $-2+5(1-5s)=3+s\Rightarrow3-25s=3+s\Rightarrow s=0$, so $t=1$.

Position vector: with $t=1$, $\mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+(-\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$; with $s=0$, $\mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$ as well. (The lines meet at $Q$.)

**The point of intersection has position vector $2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the angle between the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Direction vectors: $\mathbf{b}_1=-\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b}_2=5\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$.

$\mathbf{b}_1\cdot\mathbf{b}_2=(-1)(5)+(5)(1)=0.$

The scalar product is zero, so $\cos\varphi=0$ and $\varphi=90^\circ$.

**The lines are perpendicular: the angle between them is $90^\circ$.**
